bips_prs.title: BIP352: add taproot key-path spend with annex vector
bips_prs.body: Add a BIP-352 test vector where a taproot input is spent via the key path with an annex (2-item witness). The annex must be stripped before deciding between key-path and script-path spends, so the input is still eligible and all expected values match the plain key-path case.

nodes.body:
Concept ACK

Agree with @fametrano's stronger annex (0x50 + BIP-341 NUMS point H), see suggestions below.

btclib-wallet, a BIP352 implementation I maintain, reproduces the new vector at 48493fa: sending and receiving both match the expected values.

I ran its BIP352 tests at commit 3b88201 with this file in place of its copy of the vectors, and all tests on the new vector pass.

The vector does not catch a missing annex strip, though. With the strip removed from btclib-wallet, those tests still pass: the annex `0x5000` is taken for a control block, but not one with the NUMS internal key, so the input stays eligible. With the annex set to `0x50` followed by BIP341's NUMS key H, `0x5050929b74c1a04954b78b4b6035e97a5e078a5a0f28ec96d547bfee9ace803ac0`, the same change fails on both sending and receiving, and the unmodified code still matches the expected values. Only the witness changes; its signature has to be redone, since BIP341 signs the annex.

With the annex set to `0x50` followed by BIP341's NUMS key H, `0x5050929b74c1a04954b78b4b6035e97a5e078a5a0f28ec96d547bfee9ace803ac0`, the same change fails on both sending and receiving, and the unmodified code still matches the expected values. Only the witness changes; its signature has to be redone, since BIP341 signs the annex.

Thanks for the review. Done!

LGTM, can you rebase on master (this PR branch is still based on BIP-352 version 1.1.0 from March), and add a small changelog entry with bumped PATCH version? (see e.g. https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pull/2142 for an example).

bips_prs.title: bip352: fix up undefined index in Overview section
bips_prs.body:
Notation-only changes to the overview section. They are:

P<sub>i</sub> -> P<sub>k</sub>. The index i is never defined, and the output is derived from the counter k.

Define A = a·G right after a is redefined as the sum of the input private keys. Then use A in input_hash = hash(outpoint<sub>L</sub> || A) instead of (a·G). The BIP uses uppercase for public keys, and this was the only place where a public key appeared in the middle of an operation as (a·G). It also matches the sender spec, which writes "A = a·G".

nodes.body: ACK, thank you for the rapid responses.
Thanks for the rapid response and review as well!

core_pr.title: Silent Payments: Implement bip352 (take 2)
core_pr.body:
This PR is part of integrating silent payments into Bitcoin Core. It is the second iteration of https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28122, now based on https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1765.

This project is tracked in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/28536.

BIP352
This PR focuses strictly on the BIP logic and attempts to separate it from the wallet and transaction implementation details. This is accomplished by working directly with public and private keys, instead of needing a wallet backend and transactions for testing. Labels for the receiver are optional and thus deferred for a later PR.

Test vectors from the BIP are included as unit tests.
